messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph).
• In cities: 25–35 mph.
• Rural roads: 55 mph unless posted otherwise. | Speed limits can be lower in construction zones or school zones. | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Children under 5 must be in a rear‑facing seat. | Failure to buckle up can result in a $50 fine. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Lower BAC limits for commercial drivers (0.04 %) and drivers under 21 (0.02 %).
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, possible jail time. | Texas has a “zero‑tolerance” policy for drivers under 21. | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Violations carry a $50 fine. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right yields.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks.
• School buses stopping to pick up/drop off children must have all lanes stopped. | Failure to yield can lead to fines and points on your license. | | **Headlights & Lighting** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Fog lights are allowed only when visibility is ≤ 200 ft. | Improper lighting can result in a $50 fine. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must display valid registration stickers.
• Towing a vehicle requires a valid license and insurance. | Unregistered vehicles can be impounded. | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of fire hydrants, driveways, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a handicap space without a valid permit is a $200 fine. | Parking violations can lead to towing. | | **Traffic Signals & Signs** | • Red light = stop; green light = go; yellow light = prepare to stop.
• Stop signs require a full stop. | Running a red light can lead to a $200 fine and points. | | **Points System** | • Accumulating 4 points in 2 years can lead to license suspension.
• Points are added for violations like speeding, DUI, reckless driving, etc. | Points can be reduced through defensive‑driving courses. | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for total bodily injury, $25,000 for property damage. | Driving without insurance can lead to license suspension and civil penalties. | | **Special Zones** | • School zones: speed limit 25 mph; reduced limits during school hours.
• Construction zones: posted signs may lower speed limits. | Violations in these zones can carry higher fines. | ### Quick Resources - **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – [https://www.dps.texas.gov/](https://www.dps.texas.gov/) - **Texas Transportation Code** – online legal text for detailed statutes. - **Texas Driver Handbook** – downloadable PDF with all rules and regulations. If you need more specific information (e.g., penalties for a particular offense, recent changes to the law, or how to appeal a ticket), let me know!
